text:
maya: Quick heads-up — the Go generator quickstart sampleapp leaks goroutines if you hit an auth token refresh mid-stream and call Resume(). Repro steps inlined.

maya: Steps to repro: 1) start generator stream from sampleapp, 2) expire token, 3) SDK auto-refreshes and Resume() called by user code, 4) generator background retry goroutine keeps running and never exits.

sam: Oof. Is the issue that we spawn a retry goroutine without binding to the request ctx?

alex: Yep. Found the root cause — in sampleapp we use a long-lived context for the stream and then call Resume() which starts a detached retry routine. If parent ctx is context.Background() the goroutine can't be cancelled.

alex: Minimal fix: ensure resume uses the same ctx and that the quickstart shows a context.WithCancel or WithTimeout. Example we should add to sampleapp:

alex: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 45*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Generator().Start(ctx, genOpts)
if err != nil { return err }
// read tokens until done, or ctx cancellation
for token := range stream.Tokens() {
  fmt.Print(token.Text)
}
stream.Close()
```

alex: And in the SDK we should change Resume to accept a ctx param: Resume(ctx context.Context) so callers can propagate cancellation.

maya: Love that. Short-term patch: update quickstart to use ctx with cancel and add a comment about Resume semantics.

ci-bot: deployment pipeline:ci triggered for branch fix/gen-resume-cancel

sam: Also adding unit test to simulate token refresh and assert no goroutine leaks (use runtime.NumGoroutine + backoff loop).

maya: Can someone pick the quickstart PR? Small change + comment. I'll write the blurb for the onboarding doc explaining expected Resume behavior and link to SDK PR after.

alex: I'll open the SDK PR for Resume(ctx) and a small compat shim Resume() that forwards to Resume(context.Background()) to avoid breaking users.

maya: :thumbsup: Thanks team — this should reduce onboarding friction a lot.
